channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency hit by job cuts
item.description: The union representing most of the Canadian Food Inspection Agency staff warned of potential food safety concerns after workers learned of coming job cuts.

item.title: Bank of Canada holds rates, says hard to predict future moves
item.description: The Bank of Canada on Wednesday held its policy rate at 2.25 per cent, as widely expected, and Governor Tiff Macklem said the high level of uncertainty made it difficult to predict when and how rates might next change.

item.title: ADM to pay $40 million in U.S. SEC settlement, avoids criminal charges
item.description: Grain trader Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (ADM) has agreed to pay a $40 million (C$54.2 million) civil penalty to settle charges from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it inflated the performance of a key business segment.

item.title: New canola hybrids make better use of nitrogen
item.description: WINNIPEG — A lot depends on soil moisture and environmental conditions, but canola is becoming more efficient at pulling nitrogen out of the soil, says Jennifer Sabourin, an agronomist in St. Jean Baptiste, Man. item.title: Organic research program cut
item.description: The organic sector says the loss of research at Swift Current, Sask., will set the industry back, and it urged the federal agriculture minister to walk back the cuts.

item.title: Market response to China-Canada deal has been mixed
item.description: Cash prices will strengthen as Chinese buying boosts export demand. Keep this in mind as you formulate your marketing plan for canola for the second half of the crop year.

item.title: Paper changes to help readers
item.description: Farmers know better than anyone that the ability to adapt to changing conditions is essential for a successful business. This has never been truer than right now.

item.title: Prairie Wheat Weekly: Prices climb in most locales
item.description: Western Canadian cash prices for spring wheat and durum were mostly higher during the week ended Jan. 27, supported by gains in the United States wheat complex.

item.title: Western Canadian resentment not exceptional — or highest in country — pollster says
item.description: While Western Canada gets a lot of press for its sense of alienation from the rest of Canada, its residents’ resentment isn’t exceptional according to polling data from the Centre of Excellence on the Canadian Federation.

item.title: VIDEO: EZ Ballast design offers safer, more efficient tractor weight system
item.description: EZ Ballast is a system that lifts a weight into the undercarriage of a tractor instead of placing weights on the rear wheels or front of a tractor.
